UPDATE 2026-11-19. New evidence: the 10-Q and 8-K Ex99.1 for the quarter to 30-Sep-2026 (filed 4/5-Nov-2026, fetched from EDGAR; not yet in the folder's Extracted/ or Metrics CSV). Net sales 6,129 (+7%: raw-material pass-through +8%, FX +1%, divestitures -2%, volume +1%), adjusted EBITDA 883 vs 909, adjusted EBIT 689 vs 687, free cash flow (820) vs (343), net debt 14,011. Transition-period adjusted EPS guidance cut to $1.70-1.80 from $1.80-1.90 on the timing of energy and distribution cost pass-through; 31-Dec-2026 leverage now ~3.6x (was 3.5-3.6x). Management says the cost timing does not affect 2027 and reaffirmed the $650m synergy target.

ANCHORS REFRESHED: price and timestamp; FX; net debt, cash and NCI to the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet; diluted shares to the Sep-quarter EPS note; FY0 revenue rolled from FY2026 to LTM Sep-2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet does (Y1 = Oct-2026 to Sep-2027).

DRIVERS CHANGED (guidance year only): Y1 growth base 2.0 -> 3.5, bull 3.0 -> 4.5, bear 0.0 -> 2.0, because ~8% raw-material pass-through is running through sales and divestitures take ~2% off. Y1 cash-EBITDA margin base 15.0 -> 14.4, bull 15.5 -> 14.8, bear 14.8 -> 14.0: the guidance cut (~$57m pre-tax) plus dilution from zero-margin pass-through revenue. Y1 capex +0.2pp in every scenario (Sep-quarter capex 301 vs 238; LTM 4.1% of sales).

RESTATED, NOT RE-JUDGED: Y2+ margin percentages are ~0.4-0.5pp lower (base terminal 15.3 -> 14.9, bull 17.0 -> 16.6, bear 14.5 -> 14.0) purely so that Y2+ cash EBITDA DOLLARS match the prior paths rolled forward one quarter; the pass-through revenue carries no margin. Base cash EBITDA: Y2 3,726 vs prior 3,711, Y4 4,006 vs prior 3,989.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and what would move each: Y2-Y10 growth rates (a second quarter of positive organic volume, or resin prices reverting, which would cut revenue without cutting EBITDA); SBC % path (10-K/T grant disclosure); D&A 3.7% and Y2+ capex 3.8%/3.9% (calendar-2027 capex guidance); cash tax ramp 19% -> 21% (Sep-quarter tax paid of 42 vs 105 is timing); working-capital capture -10%; WACC 7.8%; terminal growth and the 15x owner-FCF cap; the 25/50/25 weights (see weights_rationale).
Growth is not extrapolated from reported history: FY2025 and FY2026 revenue jumps are the all-stock Berry merger (closed 30-Apr-2025). Pro-forma combined revenue was roughly flat FY2024-FY2026.

Base-year earnings use the company's adjusted basis (excludes restructuring/integration, acquired-intangible amortisation 558/yr, hyperinflation), haircut by the 'Other' cash line. D&A 3.7% excludes acquired-intangible amortisation. Remaining Berry Plan integration cash cost (~31 in the quarter, plan total 280) is treated as non-recurring and left out, as is any divestiture proceeds from the ~$2.5bn portfolio review.

Bear-case entry price at the 15% hurdle is NEGATIVE: with ~14bn of net debt, the bear flows discounted at 15% do not cover the debt. This is a leverage artefact of demanding 15% from an asset valued at 7.8%, not a solvency forecast; terminal value does not hit the zero floor in any scenario (the 15x cap binds in all three).
Share counts and per-share figures are all post the 1-for-5 reverse split of 14-Jan-2026.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: pro-forma organic revenue (0-2%) plus synergy-driven earnings growth; NOT the equity CAGR (all-stock Berry merger issued $10.4bn of equity) and NOT the reported revenue/FCF CAGRs (acquisition-inflated)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 19.6% vs revenue 12.8% vs GAAP EPS -4.6%: all three are distorted by the April-2025 all-stock Berry merger (FY2025 has 2 months of Berry, FY2026 the first full year) and the 1-for-5 consolidation of 14-Jan-2026. Pro-forma combined revenue FY2025->FY2026 was +1.1% reported, ~-2% organic (10-K MD&A: +52% acquired, +5% FX, +2% raw-material pass-through, -2% volume/mix). Per-share owner FCF fell ~3%/yr over five years (US$3.00 -> US$2.54 post-split) -- the merger has so far added scale, not per-share cash. The selected 2.5% is a forward judgment, not a historical fit.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC add-back - cash tax withholding on net-share settlement (FY2024 3, FY2025 75, FY2026 42; earlier years 0 -- Amcor settled from treasury purchases, which are value-neutral under the flat-count convention). 5yr owner-FCF CAGR 4.7% vs reported 5.6%: SBC roughly doubled with Berry's equity plans. Adjusted EPS is the company's non-GAAP series restated for the 1-for-5 consolidation (FY2021 74.1c -> $3.705 etc.); GAAP EPS is the 10-K's restated series. Diluted share counts pre-FY2025 are the reported figures / 5.

base.ebitda_margin_note: CASH-ADJUSTED EBITDA margin: company adjusted EBITDA less the recurring 'Other' operating cash line (~156/yr: pension funding above expense and similar). LTM Sep-2026 actual 14.6% (adjusted EBITDA 3,647 less 156 = 3,491 on revenue 23,890). Add ~0.6pp to compare with the company's adjusted EBITDA margin. Percentages are ~0.4pp lower than the 2026-09-21 version for the same EBITDA dollars because ~2.5% of forward revenue is now zero-margin raw-material pass-through.
base.narrative: The energy and distribution cost squeeze that cut transition-period guidance is a timing issue, as management says, but not all of the lost margin comes back: cash EBITDA grows ~2% in the first twelve months (Oct-2026 to Sep-2027) and the margin recovers from 14.4% to 14.9% by Y4 (company adjusted basis ~15.5%), which is the prior version's dollar path with about a quarter of the remaining Berry synergies reaching the bottom line. Reported revenue runs +3.5% in Y1 on raw-material pass-through, then 2.5-3% nominal; the first positive organic volume in three years (+1%, focus categories +3%) is taken as stabilisation, not acceleration. The ~$2.5bn portfolio review is value-neutral. Cash tax ramps 19% -> 21%. Leverage peaks seasonally near 3.75x and falls toward 3x through 2027-28; no re-rating is assumed, with the exit held at 15x owner FCF (~8x terminal EBITDA).

bull.narrative: Synergies deliver in full ($650m by mid-2028), the energy and freight costs are fully recovered in 2027 pricing, and North America beverage and the other non-core units are exited or fixed, so the retained portfolio's cash margin reaches 16.6% (company basis ~17.2%). The September-quarter volume turn proves durable: pet food, foodservice, healthcare and beauty mix push organic volume to +1.5-2% and revenue compounds 4-4.5%. The Middle-East working-capital build unwinds, deleveraging arrives early and buybacks resume. Terminal growth 3.0%, still capped at 15x FCF.

Percentages are ~0.4pp lower than the 2026-09-21 version for the same EBITDA dollars because ~2.5% of forward revenue is now zero-margin raw-material pass-through.
bear.narrative: The cost pass-through lag is not timing: energy, freight and resin stay elevated, consolidating CPG customers resist recovery, and the remaining synergies are conceded in price, so the cash margin sits at 14.0% (pre-merger Amcor's ~14.5% on a revenue base inflated by pass-through). Volumes slip back to -1 to -2% after one good quarter; reported revenue grows 2% in Y1 only because of resin prices, then 0.5-1.5%. The working-capital build does not reverse, leverage stays at or above 3.6x against a 3.9x covenant, the dividend (~$1.2bn) absorbs all levered free cash flow, and the portfolio review drags without a clean exit. A slow-erosion case with a dividend or covenant question attached, not an insolvency case. Terminal growth 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25, UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-21 version (house default is 15/50/35). Bear stays at 25%: guidance was cut again, the quarter's free cash outflow was 820 and covenant headroom is thin at a seasonal peak (~3.75x vs 3.9x; undrawn revolver down to $1.32bn), but that is offset by the first positive organic volume in three years and reaffirmed synergy and 2027 commentary. Base 50%. Bull stays at 25% because it still needs three independent things: full synergy delivery, a clean non-core exit and sustained positive volume. What would move it: 31-Dec-2026 leverage above the ~3.6x guide or a covenant amendment -> bear 30-35%; a second quarter of positive volume with the working-capital build reversing -> toward 20/50/30.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Amcor remains a slow-growing, defensive, heavily levered packaging consolidator whose next three years are a synergy and deleveraging story. This update changes little in the operating view and a lot in the anchors, which largely cancel: the weaker AUD adds about A$4.2 per share, the 1.1bn rise in net debt over the September quarter takes about A$3.8 away, and the guidance cut, higher first-year capex and base-period roll take a net A$1.3. The result is that the shares sit a few percent above the weighted value and almost exactly between the house and street bases: roughly fairly valued, as before. It is an income-plus-deleveraging holding, not a compounder; the 15% hurdle is unreachable at any plausible price because more than 40% of enterprise value is debt, and the bear-case hurdle price is below zero.
key_judgments: FY0 is LTM Sep-2026 and the balance sheet is 30-Sep-2026, so flows and bridge share one date; the seasonal September cash trough needs no adjustment because Y1 spans a full cycle.
The abnormal resin-driven working-capital build (~500) is left in net debt and not credited back; the remaining integration cash cost and any divestiture proceeds are also left out.
Later-year EBITDA dollars are the prior judgments; only the margin percentages were restated for pass-through revenue.
WACC 7.8% including a 0.5% leverage/integration premium, identical across scenarios; scenario risk lives in the flows and the 25% bear weight.
Exit capped at 15x owner FCF (~8x terminal EBITDA), binding in all three scenarios: no re-rating is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: ~3.75x at the seasonal peak against a 3.9x covenant; every 500 of net debt is about A$1.6 per share.
Cost pass-through: whether energy, freight and resin inflation is recovered in 2027 pricing is the difference between the base and bear margin paths.
Cash conversion: FY2026 free cash flow was guided down twice and the September quarter outflow was 820.
AUDUSD: a 5% move in the rate moves every AUD value here by about 5%; the model's USD values are unaffected.
Execution load: Berry integration, fiscal-year change, Miami HQ move and auditor change running concurrently.
The six-month transition period means no clean 12-month comparable until calendar 2027 is reported in early 2028.
